references.text: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke because the Lord had descended on it in fire. This describes the same divine revelation on the mountain where God spoke from the fire.
The prohibition against making carved images or any representation. This is directly linked to the fact that the people saw no form when God spoke to them.
God tells Moses that no human can see his face and live. This confirms why the people saw no form at Horeb.
The Lord spoke to you out of the fire, and you heard the words but saw no form, only a voice. This is the immediate context explaining verse 15.
The Lord spoke with you face to face on the mountain, out of the fire. This repeats the event at Horeb where God revealed himself through fire.
These words the Lord spoke to the entire assembly on the mountain, out of the fire and the cloud and the darkness. Confirms God's speech from the fire without a visible form.
With whom will you compare God, and what image will you liken him to? Isaiah challenges idolatry based on God's incomparable nature.
No one has ever seen God. The only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known. Confirms God's invisible nature, revealed only through the Son.
The Father who sent me has himself testified about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form. Jesus confirms that no one has seen God's form.
To the eternal King, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever! Paul affirms God's invisible nature.
He who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no human has seen or can see. Confirms that no one can see God.
